selected.rationale: Killing the sole ingress proxy makes every API request fail, exposing the single-point-of-entry availability weakness with no failover.
Compose-post is the orchestrator for all post creation; killing it takes down the entire write path and reveals no recovery or fallback.
Post-storage is a shared dependency of both compose-post and home-timeline; its loss breaks write and read paths, confirming an availability weakness in persistent storage.
Delaying the critical post-storage write blocks every compose-post call; without timeouts, this causes unbounded latency propagation and thread exhaustion.
A dropped fanout to home-timeline lets compose-post return success while followers never receive the post, confirming missing retries and data inconsistency.
Home-timeline must wait on social-graph for every read; a delay without timeouts stalls all timeline reads and exposes the absence of timeout/retry defenses.
Killing home-timeline impacts both the compose fanout and the read API, causing availability loss in multiple user-facing flows.
Loss between home-timeline and post-storage produces incomplete timeline reads for many users, showing missing retry behavior on the read path.
A lost unique-id request prevents post composition from completing, confirming the lack of retry defense on a required write dependency.
Delay in updating the user timeline propagates back to compose-post, inflating write latency and increasing the risk of thread-pool saturation.
